data.note:
Specimen s_f0826fee65 correctly identified as Eg5 inhibitor class (AZ138, BBBC021 annotation Eg5 inhibitors). 

**Reflection:**
- NSC protocol vote was decisive: 3/4 acquired wells (0.3, 1.0, 3.0 µM) nearest to Eg5 reference (AZ-C) with similarities 0.79-0.80 (e9), and 7/10 k-nearest neighbors were Eg5 inhibitors (mean similarity 0.769). The 10 µM well voted Actin disruptors at low similarity (0.52) consistent with toxicity/empty fields, not class.
- Phenotype fit Eg5 inhibition: dose-dependent monotonic increases in tub_mean (rho=+1.0, e10, z 21.2 at 0.3 µM to 103.7 at 10 µM) and frac_mitotic_like (rho=+1.0, e11, z 2.4 to 159.0, 65% mitotic-like at 10 µM), with condensed small nuclei (nuc_major_axis z -21.5, e3), reduced cell count and bright yellow round monopolar-like asters on near-empty background at high dose (e5). Microscopist suggested Microtubule stabilizers based on tubulin brightening, but this is expected secondary to mitotic arrest and aster formation; destabilizers were ruled out by increased (not decreased) tub intensity (e2,e7,e8).
- External validation: PubChem/ChEMBL lookup for AZ138 returned no curated mechanism, as expected for a tool compound; BBBC021 annotation is Eg5 inhibitors, matching the NSC call. Literature on human KSP/Eg5 inhibition establishes monopolar spindle formation and mitotic arrest as the hallmark phenotype of this class (e.g., mechanism of KSP inhibition by monastrol, PMID:15568818). No additional PMID for AZ138 itself was retrieved, but the atlas neighbor identity and dose-responsive mitotic arrest together provide convergent evidence.

reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: Eg5 inhibitors (AZ138, compound lookup failed in PubChem/ChEMBL – no structure to verify, scored by protocol 1-NN per well majority vote). My final call Eg5 inhibitors p=0.78 was correct and protocol vote was 3/4 wells Eg5 with summed similarity 2.386 vs 1/4 Actin disruptors 0.52. Review was approve.

What the evidence got right: The discriminative signal was in the non-toxic range 0.3, 1.0 and 3.0 µM – wells w_90ab9f5afc, w_5868a4e8e5, w_894a4c20d7. All three gave consistent nearest-MOA Eg5 inhibitors with similarities 0.797, 0.788, 0.801 in the per-well protocol, and k-NN 6/10 -> 7/10 Eg5 on comparison to reference atlas e4/e9. The measurements driving this were not subtle: tub_mean z +21.2 at 0.3 µM, +26.4 at 1 µM, +29.5 at 3 µM with dose_response rho=+1.00 p=0, and frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0, both over the 4 non-toxic wells e10/e11. Cell counts stayed high 485, 356, 469 cells in those wells, so the tubulin rise is well sampled, not a toxicity artifact. This is the classic Eg5/KSP phenotype – monopolar spindle arrest concentrates tubulin signal and increases mitotic fraction without true microtubule polymerization, as described for KSP inhibition by monastrol PMID 15568818. 

Equally important was what argued against alternatives: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 argues against Aurora B polyploidy, and tub_mean increase argues against Microtubule destabilizers which I had initially kept at p=0.10. That allowed e14 to demote both destabilizers to 0.04 and Aurora to 0.03 and correctly reinterpret tub_mean not as stabilizer polymerization but as mitotic accumulation. actin signals act_std z +33.0 to +39.7 and act_glcm_contrast z +29.5 to +42.3 across e2/e7/e8 were initially ambiguous but in retrospect are rounded mitotic cells, not primary actin disruption – consistent with the high-dose well w_4c0c203d43 being called Actin disruptors at low similarity 0.52 only when toxic.

What misled me and why: Two sources. 1) Acquisition choice e3: sampling 10 µM rep1 very early. That well had only 28 cells measured, tub_glcm_contrast z=+203.0, frac_mitotic_like z=+159.0, act_glcm_contrast z=+144.1 – extreme, saturated z-scores from a dying population. Protocol correctly down-weighted it (similarity 0.52 vs ~0.80 for the other three) but my early update e6 still gave Microtubule stabilizers 0.40 vs Eg5 0.35 based on 1/2 NSC vote, explicitly citing the visual phenotype e5. 2) describe_phenotype e5: microscopist on 4 fields said density lower vs DMSO and candidates: Microtubule stabilizers. This reinforced tub_mean increase as stabilizer-like and caused me to write in e14 rationale tub rise is mitotic arrest not polymerization, but I only arrived there after acquiring the bridging doses 0.3 and 3.0 µM e7/e8.

What I missed / acquisition bias: I mapped 8 doses 0.01-30 µM but chose only moderate then high (1 µM then 10 µM) before filling the onset range. That put a toxic outlier with high toxicity and weak attribution into the first atlas comparison. If this were a real lab I would have excluded w_4c0c203d43 from MoA voting due to <50 cells and required n>200 for NSC, and sampled 0.03-0.1 µM to define baseline before committing to e6 weights. Literature search for AZ138 Eg5 KSP inhibitor e16 returned 0 hits, so I had no compound-level confirmation and had to rely purely on phenotype vs the generic Eg5 KSP inhibition monopolar spindle mitotic arrest literature e17.

Lesson: For mitotic MoAs, dose-dependent tub_mean + frac_mitotic_like with stable cell counts 300-500 is more informative than absolute z magnitude in a toxic well. Next experiment as proposed remains valid: high-resolution tubulin/DNA imaging for spindle polarity quantification plus pHH3 across 0.03-3 µM vs Eg5 and stabilizer references to directly confirm monopolar vs bipolar spindles.
